summary: Frontend-only verification of MeasurementWorksheet Office 'Needs Review' 409 flow. All required UI behaviors PASSED: (1) banner appears on 409, (2) Save button disabled/blocked while needsReview set (repeated clicks cannot bypass), (3) 'Keep My Version' shows inline confirmation warning with exact required text, Cancel returns to two-option state, Confirm saves successfully and clears banner (server persisted the local edit), (4) 'Use Latest Version' adopts server revision, discards local edits (verified structure name reverted to server value), clears banner, and does NOT overwrite the server. However, a CRITICAL backend serialization bug was discovered while validating the flow: measurement PUT endpoints return updated_at as a Pydantic-serialized ISO string ending in 'Z' (e.g. 2026-09-02T03:19:51.509754Z), but the server compares If-Match against rev.updated_at.isoformat() which produces '+00:00' (e.g. 2026-09-02T03:19:51.509754+00:00). Because these strings never match, EVERY UI save results in a spurious 409, even without any concurrent change. The Keep My Version path only works because the 409 detail body is generated via fastapi.encoders.jsonable_encoder (which uses '+00:00' format) — so re-saving with detail.server.updated_at DOES match and succeeds. Net effect for a real user: they cannot save any normal edit; every Save immediately triggers Needs Review even in single-actor use.

critical.issue: If-Match token format mismatch — GET/PUT response serializes updated_at as ISO with 'Z' suffix (Pydantic), but server compares to rev.updated_at.isoformat() which yields '+00:00'. Result: every save from the UI 409s spuriously. Repro (curl): GET returns updated_at '2026-09-02T03:19:51.509754Z'; PUT with If-Match=that -> 409; PUT with If-Match=2026-09-02T03:19:51.509754+00:00 -> 200. Fix: normalize both sides — either serialize the datetime with '+00:00' (jsonable_encoder-style) in MeasurementRevisionOut for updated_at, OR compare tokens tolerantly (parse both to datetime and compare). Recommend: add a computed string field 'updated_at' serialized identically to jsonable_encoder(rev.updated_at) so client copies always round-trip.

action_items: Fix backend PUT /api/measurements/{id} If-Match comparison: normalize updated_at serialization so the token round-trips (client sees the SAME string that the server compares against). Suggested fix in backend/services/measurements.py build_out(): return updated_at as jsonable_encoder(rev.updated_at) (ISO with '+00:00'), OR change router If-Match check to parse both sides to datetime and compare tz-aware equality.

After backend fix, retest the entire worksheet Save flow (non-conflict Save should succeed and NOT show Needs Review), then re-run the concurrent-change scenario to confirm 409 fires only on genuine conflicts.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/measurements.py L75-78: If-Match token derived from rev.updated_at.isoformat() but response serialization for updated_at (Pydantic v2 default) emits 'Z' suffix. Single source of truth is required — either send jsonable_encoder-format updated_at to the client or parse the token before compare.
The current code SILENTLY makes single-user Office saves impossible; only Keep-My-Version accidentally works because its second attempt uses the freshly-jsonable_encoded token from the 409 body.
MeasurementWorksheet.jsx correctly implements the Needs Review UX (guard on save, banner, both resolution buttons, warning gate) and passes all 4 requirement criteria.

rca of the issue: Root cause: dual serialization paths for datetime in FastAPI. (1) MeasurementRevisionOut Pydantic model serializes updated_at using pydantic-core v2 default, which emits 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ'. (2) The 409 detail body is built with fastapi.encoders.jsonable_encoder(out) which serializes datetime via isoformat() -> 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff+00:00'. (3) The server-side compare uses rev.updated_at.isoformat() -> '+00:00'. Client stores response updated_at unchanged and echoes it back as If-Match; the 'Z' form never equals the '+00:00' form. Repro (curl): PUT with If-Match=response.updated_at → 409; PUT with If-Match=response.updated_at with 'Z' replaced by '+00:00' → 200. Mitigation: make one canonical format for updated_at across GET and 409 detail (recommended: jsonable_encoder style '+00:00'). Alternatively, in the router, parse the incoming If-Match with datetime.fromisoformat (accepting trailing Z by replacing with '+00:00' or using dateutil) and compare as datetime objects.
